title: HYD G+Y SYS LO PR

alert.trigger: This alert triggers when the green and yellow systems pressure ≤1 450 PSI (the alert resets if pressure ≥1 750 PSI).

effectivity.note: One FCOM procedure for all HS-TX.

summary: A red warning with red LAND ASAP: green and yellow hydraulics are lost. The FCTM says a MAYDAY should be declared, and the ECAM actions should be completed before the approach. No AP, alternate law with protections lost, no flaps and no stabilizer. The key point: stabilize at VAPP in CONF 3 before the gravity gear extension, because direct law then freezes the pitch trim reference and the manual trim is unusable. No reversers, no nosewheel steering, and braking on the yellow accumulator only.

background.text: The stabilizer is lost. In alternate law, the auto trim function is provided through the elevators. At landing gear extension, switching to direct law, the auto trim is lost, and the mean elevator position at that time is memorized and becomes the reference for the centered sidestick position.

The PTU must be switched off without delay when required by the ECAM for reservoir low level, low air pressure (only if pressure fluctuates) or overheat, to avoid a PTU overheat that may lead to the loss of the second circuit.
Pitch: with HYD G+Y, alternate law has reduced protections; direct law applies in roll; yaw is mechanical.

technique.text: A double hydraulic failure is an emergency, with red LAND ASAP displayed; a MAYDAY should be declared. Land as soon as possible, but complete the ECAM actions before the approach.
It is a "complex procedure": refer to the QRH summary when the ECAM procedure is complete. A clear reading of STATUS is essential to sequence the actions during the approach.

Wait for stabilization at VAPP before the gear extension, to ensure a proper centered sidestick position for approach and landing. If this is missed, the flare and pitch control in a go-around may be difficult. Disregard the PFD message USE MAN PITCH TRIM after gear extension.
High pitch during the approach should be expected: outline it in the arrival briefing for tail strike awareness, and monitor pitch attitude during the flare.

gaps.text: The FCTM and PDP give the sequence but no PF/PM slide for this failure: the turns come from the AOP-20 task sharing, FCTM AOP-30-60 and the QRH summary. The manuals do not say who turns the handcrank; the PM is shown from instructor practice.
The MAYDAY wording is not given in the supplied manuals.
QRH fuel penalty factor for G+Y SYS LO PR is 0 % to 10 % for all HS-TX (stabilizer jammed, spoilers 1, 2, 4 and 5); the FMS predictions are unreliable.
